claim: Human chromosomes terminate in telomeres, which are repetitive DNA sequences bound by the shelterin complex.
source: Human chromosomes terminate in telomeres, repetitive DNA sequences bound by the shelterin complex.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by the citation to Blackburn, 2005.

claim: Shelterin protects chromosome ends and prevents recognition by the DNA damage machinery.
source: Shelterin protects chromosome ends, prevents recognition by the DNA damage machinery, and recruits telomerase.
evidence: This is supported by reference to Palm & de Lange, 2008.

claim: Shelterin recruits telomerase to telomeres.
source: Shelterin protects chromosome ends, prevents recognition by the DNA damage machinery, and recruits telomerase.
evidence: This is supported by reference to Palm & de Lange, 2008.

claim: The TEL-patch on the OB-fold domain of TPP1 is essential to recruit telomerase to telomeres.
source: A patch of amino acids, termed the TEL-patch, on the OB-fold domain of the shelterin component TPP1 is essential to recruit telomerase to telomeres.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work.

claim: The site on telomerase that interacts with the TPP1 OB-fold is not well defined.
source: In contrast, the site on telomerase that interacts with the TPP1 OB-fold is not well defined.
evidence: This statement sets up the research question addressed in the study.

claim: Separation-of-function mutations in the TEN-domain of hTERT disrupt the interaction of telomerase with TPP1 in vivo and in vitro but have very little effect on catalytic activity.
source: In this study, we identify separation-of-function mutations in the TEN-domain of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) that disrupt the interaction of telomerase with TPP1 in vivo and in vitro but have very little effect on the catalytic activity of telomerase.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Suppression of a TEN-domain mutation with a compensatory charge-swap mutation in the TEL-patch indicates that the association between the TEN-domain and TEL-patch is direct.
source: Suppression of a TEN-domain mutation with a compensatory charge-swap mutation in the TEL-patch indicates that their association is direct.
evidence: This is a key finding supported by the charge-swap experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chromosome ends shorten progressively each cell cycle due to the end-replication problem.
source: Chromosome ends pose two challenges to cells: they resemble DNA damage sites, and they shorten progressively each cell cycle due to the end-replication problem (Levy et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Levy et al., 1992.

claim: Telomerase is an RNA-containing reverse transcriptase that adds telomeric repeats to the 3ʹ-end of the single-stranded overhang to maintain telomere length.
source: Additionally, shelterin recruits telomerase, an RNA-containing reverse transcriptase that adds telomeric repeats to the 3ʹ-end of the single-stranded overhang to maintain telomere length (Nandakumar and Cech, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nandakumar and Cech, 2013.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in telomerase and shelterin components cause human diseases like dyskeratosis congenita, aplastic anemia, and pulmonary fibrosis.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in telomerase and shelterin components cause human diseases like dyskeratosis congenita, aplastic anemia, and pulmonary fibrosis (Armanios and Blackburn, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Armanios and Blackburn, 2012.

claim: 90% of cancers depend on telomerase activity to maintain the potential to proliferate indefinitely.
source: In addition, like stem cells and germ cells, 90% of cancers depend on telomerase activity to maintain the potential to proliferate indefinitely (Stewart and Weinberg, 2006; Shay and Wright, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Stewart and Weinberg, 2006 and Shay and Wright, 2011.

claim: The catalytic core of telomerase is comprised of hTERT and the telomerase RNA component (hTR).
source: Its catalytic core is comprised of hTERT and the telomerase RNA component (hTR), which contains the template used for telomeric DNA synthesis (Cech, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cech, 2004.

claim: hTR contains the template used for telomeric DNA synthesis.
source: Its catalytic core is comprised of hTERT and the telomerase RNA component (hTR), which contains the template used for telomeric DNA synthesis (Cech, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cech, 2004.

claim: In the holoenzyme, hTR associates with dyskerin for stability and with TCAB1 for telomerase maturation and trafficking to Cajal bodies.
source: In the holoenzyme, hTR also associates with dyskerin for stability and with TCAB1 for telomerase maturation and trafficking to Cajal bodies (Mitchell et al., 1999; Venteicher et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mitchell et al., 1999 and Venteicher et al., 2009.

claim: The hTERT protein contains four domains: the TEN-domain, TRBD, RT-domain, and CTE.
source: The hTERT protein contains four domains, the telomerase N-terminal domain (TEN-domain), the telomerase RNA-binding domain (TRBD), the reverse transcriptase domain (RT-domain), and the C-terminal extension (CTE) or putative thumb domain of the reverse transcriptase.
evidence: This is a description of the domain structure of hTERT.

claim: The TRBD- and RT-domains of hTERT bind hTR and position the template of hTR in the RT-domain active site to synthesize telomeric repeats.
source: The TRBD- and RT-domains of hTERT bind hTR and position the template of hTR in the RT-domain active site to synthesize telomeric repeats (Cech, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cech, 2004.

claim: The TEN-domain participates in the catalysis of telomeric repeat addition.
source: The TEN-domain participates in the catalysis of telomeric repeat addition (Jacobs et al., 2006; Jurczyluk et al., 2011; Robart and Collins, 2011; Wu and Collins, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jacobs et al., 2006; Jurczyluk et al., 2011; Robart and Collins, 2011; Wu and Collins, 2014.

claim: Both the TEN-domain and CTE contain DAT regions (N-DAT and C-DAT, respectively).
source: Additionally, both the TEN-domain and CTE contain DAT (dissociates activities of telomerase) regions, N-DAT and C-DAT, respectively (Armbruster et al., 2001; Banik et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Armbruster et al., 2001 and Banik et al., 2002.

claim: Mutations in either DAT-region disrupt the ability of telomerase to immortalize cells, but they retain catalytic activity.
source: Mutations in either DAT-region disrupt the ability of telomerase to immortalize cells, but they retain catalytic activity (Armbruster et al., 2001; Banik et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Armbruster et al., 2001 and Banik et al., 2002.

claim: Based on experiments with N-DAT mutants, the TEN-domain has been proposed to mediate telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
source: Based on experiments with N-DAT mutants, the TEN-domain has been proposed to mediate telomerase recruitment to telomeres (Armbruster et al., 2003, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Armbruster et al., 2003, 2004.

claim: Telomerase is recruited to telomeres in S-phase, while it remains in Cajal bodies for the remainder of the cell cycle.
source: Telomerase is recruited to telomeres in S-phase, while it remains in Cajal bodies for the remainder of the cell cycle (Jady et al., 2006; Tomlinson et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jady et al., 2006 and Tomlinson et al., 2006.

claim: Telomerase localization to Cajal bodies requires the interaction of hTR with TCAB1.
source: Telomerase localization to Cajal bodies requires the interaction of hTR with TCAB1 (Venteicher et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Venteicher et al., 2009.

claim: TCAB1 is not required for enzymatic activity but for function in vivo.
source: TCAB1 is not required for enzymatic activity but for function in vivo (Venteicher et al., 2009), indicating that recruitment to Cajal bodies is a key step in telomerase trafficking or maturation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Venteicher et al., 2009.

claim: Recruitment of telomerase to the telomere requires the shelterin component TPP1.
source: Recruitment of telomerase to the telomere requires the shelterin component TPP1 (Xin et al., 2007; Abreu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xin et al., 2007 and Abreu et al., 2010.

claim: TPP1 is recruited to the shelterin complex via an interaction with TIN2.
source: TPP1 is recruited to the shelterin complex via an interaction with TIN2 (Abreu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abreu et al., 2010.

claim: TPP1 tightly binds to POT1.
source: TPP1 also tightly binds to POT1 (Wang et al., 2007), which specifically binds the telomeric single-stranded DNA overhang (Baumann and Cech, 2001; Lei et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2007.

claim: POT1 specifically binds the telomeric single-stranded DNA overhang.
source: TPP1 also tightly binds to POT1 (Wang et al., 2007), which specifically binds the telomeric single-stranded DNA overhang (Baumann and Cech, 2001; Lei et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baumann and Cech, 2001 and Lei et al., 2004.

claim: The interaction between the POT1-TPP1 complex and telomerase stimulates its repeat addition processivity (RAP).
source: Biochemical studies have demonstrated that the interaction between the POT1-TPP1 complex and telomerase stimulates its repeat addition processivity (RAP), that is, increases the number of consecutive repeats that telomerase synthesizes in a single round of telomeric DNA addition (Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2007.

claim: The TEL-patch is a group of mostly acidic amino acids on the OB-fold domain of TPP1.
source: Recently, the TEL-patch, a group of mostly acidic amino acids on the oligosaccharide binding (OB)-fold domain of TPP1 was shown to be necessary for telomerase recruitment in vivo and RAP stimulation in vitro (Nandakumar et al., 2012; Sexton et al., 2012; Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nandakumar et al., 2012; Sexton et al., 2012; Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: The TEL-patch is necessary for telomerase recruitment in vivo and RAP stimulation in vitro.
source: Recently, the TEL-patch, a group of mostly acidic amino acids on the oligosaccharide binding (OB)-fold domain of TPP1 was shown to be necessary for telomerase recruitment in vivo and RAP stimulation in vitro (Nandakumar et al., 2012; Sexton et al., 2012; Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nandakumar et al., 2012; Sexton et al., 2012; Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: The OB-fold domain of TPP1 is sufficient to recruit telomerase to a non-telomeric chromosomal locus.
source: Furthermore, cell biological assays demonstrated that the OB-fold domain of TPP1 is sufficient to recruit telomerase to a non-telomeric chromosomal locus (Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: It has been unclear whether TPP1 makes a direct interaction with telomerase or if their interaction is bridged by another component.
source: Although TPP1 is critical for recruitment of telomerase to the telomere, it has been unclear whether TPP1 makes a direct interaction with telomerase or if their interaction is bridged by another component.
evidence: This statement sets up a key question addressed by the study.

claim: The G100V mutation in the TEN-domain of hTERT is defective in stimulation of telomerase processivity in vitro.
source: A mutation in the TEN-domain of hTERT, G100V, is defective in stimulation of telomerase processivity in vitro (Zaug et al., 2010) and fails to localize to telomeres in vivo (Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zaug et al., 2010.

claim: The G100V mutation in the TEN-domain of hTERT fails to localize to telomeres in vivo.
source: A mutation in the TEN-domain of hTERT, G100V, is defective in stimulation of telomerase processivity in vitro (Zaug et al., 2010) and fails to localize to telomeres in vivo (Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: G100V telomerase has substantially reduced enzymatic activity.
source: However, G100V telomerase has substantially reduced enzymatic activity (Zaug et al., 2010); thus, it is difficult to assess whether its failure to function in vivo is due to an activity or recruitment defect.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zaug et al., 2010.

claim: In Schizosaccharomyces pombe, Ccq1 bridges the interaction between Tpz1 (the TPP1 homologue) and telomerase.
source: In Schizosaccharomyces pombe, Ccq1 bridges the interaction between Tpz1, the TPP1 homologue, and telomerase (Miyoshi et al., 2008; Moser et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Miyoshi et al., 2008 and Moser et al., 2011.

claim: A human homologue of Ccq1 has not been identified.
source: A human homologue of Ccq1 has not been identified (Nandakumar and Cech, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nandakumar and Cech, 2013.

claim: hTERT K78E retains 92% wild-type activity and 100% processivity.
source: However, hTERT K78E retained wild-type activity and processivity (92% and 100% respectively), but RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 was reduced to 68% that of wild-type telomerase (Figure 1E–H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: hTERT K78E has RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 reduced to 68% that of wild-type telomerase.
source: However, hTERT K78E retained wild-type activity and processivity (92% and 100% respectively), but RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 was reduced to 68% that of wild-type telomerase (Figure 1E–H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The R132E mutant hTERT retained 73% activity but was defective in RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 (24% of wild-type hTERT).
source: We generated a R132E mutant hTERT, which retained moderate activity (73%) but was defective in RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 (24% of wild-type hTERT, Figure 1E–H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The K78E;R132E double mutant retained 63% activity but reduced RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 to 18% of wild-type hTERT.
source: Furthermore, the K78E;R132E double mutant retained 63% activity but further reduced RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 to 18% of wild-type hTERT (Figure 1E–H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: K78 and R132 within the TEN-domain of hTERT are in close proximity to each other, on a surface distinct from the proposed DNA-binding region of the TEN-domain.
source: An alignment of the human TEN-domain with the Tetrahymena thermophila TEN-domain in combination with a secondary structure prediction shows that K78 and R132 are in close proximity to each other, on a surface distinct from the proposed DNA-binding region of the TEN-domain (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural alignment and prediction shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: All three hTERT mutants tested (K78E, R132E, K78E;R132E) localized to bona fide Cajal bodies but did not localize to telomeres marked by TRF2.
source: In contrast, all three hTERT mutants tested (K78E, R132E, K78E;R132E) localized to bona fide Cajal bodies, forming ∼1–3 large foci per cell that co-localized with coilin but did not localize to telomeres marked by TRF2 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TEN-domain mutants that do not interact with POT1-TPP1 in vitro also fail to localize to telomeres in vivo.
source: These results demonstrate that TEN-domain mutants that do not interact with POT1-TPP1 in vitro also fail to localize to telomeres in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented.

claim: Cajal body localization of hTERT requires its association with hTR.
source: Furthermore, because Cajal body localization of hTERT requires its association with hTR, our observations indicate that telomerase assembly is unaffected by mutations in the TEN-domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutant hTERT localizes to Cajal bodies.

claim: Telomerase assembly is unaffected by mutations in the TEN-domain.
source: Furthermore, because Cajal body localization of hTERT requires its association with hTR, our observations indicate that telomerase assembly is unaffected by mutations in the TEN-domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutant hTERT localizes to Cajal bodies, which requires hTR association.

claim: TEN domain mutants K78E and R132E failed to elongate telomeres despite having telomerase enzymatic activity per cell higher than in the parental HeLa cell line.
source: In contrast, TEN domain mutants K78E and R132E failed to elongate telomeres, despite the fact that telomerase enzymatic activity per cell was higher than in the parental HeLa cell line (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: Telomerase with K78E or R132E mutations in the TEN-domain fails to elongate telomeres due to an inability to localize to telomeres, not an activity defect.
source: These observations reinforce the conclusion that telomerase with K78E or R132E mutations in the TEN-domain fails to elongate telomeres due to an inability to localize to telomeres, not an activity defect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: TPP1 E215K fully rescued the processivity defect of hTERT K78E; processivity increased from 68% to 98% relative to wild-type telomerase and wild-type TPP1.
source: Strikingly, TPP1 E215K fully rescued the processivity defect of hTERT K78E; processivity increased from 68% to 98% relative to wild-type telomerase and wild-type TPP1 (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: The non-cognate combinations of wild-type telomerase with E215K TPP1 and K78E telomerase with wild-type TPP1 showed similar reductions of RAP stimulation, to 78% and 68% of the full level, respectively.
source: Importantly, the non-cognate combinations of (i) wild-type telomerase and E215K TPP1 and (ii) K78E telomerase with wild-type TPP1 showed a similar reduction of RAP stimulation, to 78% and 68% of the full level, respectively (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: The specific and compensatory nature of the hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K mutant combination strongly suggests that K78 on the TEN-domain of hTERT directly interacts with E215 on the TEL-patch of TPP1 to stimulate RAP in vitro.
source: Thus, the specific and compensatory nature of the hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K mutant combination strongly suggests that K78 on the TEN-domain of hTERT directly interacts with E215 on the TEL-patch of TPP1 to stimulate RAP in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the charge-swap rescue experiments.

claim: The co-localization of wild-type telomerase with the E215K TPP1-OB-fold domain was greatly reduced.
source: As shown in Figure 6B,C, the co-localization of wild-type telomerase with the E215K TPP1-OB-fold domain was greatly reduced; instead, wild-type telomerase localized to many foci distinct from the LacI site, presumably telomeres.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: Introduction of the E215K mutation significantly increased the co-localization of K78E telomerase with the TPP1-OB-fold domain (p < 0.05).
source: In contrast, introduction of the E215K mutation significantly increased the co-localization of K78E telomerase with the TPP1-OB-fold domain (p < 0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data.

claim: E215K TPP1 had no effect on the localization of R132E and K78E;R132E telomerases.
source: Importantly, E215K TPP1 had no effect on the localization of R132E and K78E;R132E telomerases, demonstrating that E215K specifically compensates for the presence of the K78E mutation in hTERT (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: Finding a compensatory double mutant demonstrates that telomerase is recruited to telomeres by a direct interaction between the TEN-domain of telomerase and the TPP1-OB-fold domain in part by a contact formed between K78 in the TEN-domain and E215 in the TPP1-OB-fold domain.
source: Thus, finding a compensatory double mutant demonstrates that telomerase is recruited to telomeres by a direct interaction between the TEN-domain of telomerase and the TPP1-OB-fold domain in part by a contact formed between K78 in the TEN-domain and E215 in the TPP1-OB-fold domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the charge-swap rescue experiments in vivo.

claim: Expression of E215K TPP1 triggered a more pronounced increase in telomere length to ∼7.7 kb over 6 weeks in cells expressing K78E hTERT.
source: Importantly, expression of E215K TPP1 triggered a more pronounced increase in telomere length to ∼7.7 kb over the same time period, while E169K gave lead to a subtle increase to ∼4.9 kb.
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data.

claim: Expression of E215K TPP1 in cells expressing K78E hTERT rescues telomere length maintenance, most likely by driving telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
source: These observations demonstrate that expression of E215K TPP1 in cells expressing K78E hTERT rescues telomere length maintenance, most likely by driving telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the telomere length analysis.

claim: K78 and R132 within the TEN-domain of hTERT are critical residues that mediate the direct interaction of telomerase with the TEL-patch of TPP1, recruiting telomerase to telomeres.
source: Here, we demonstrate that K78 and R132 within the TEN-domain of hTERT are critical residues that mediate the direct interaction of telomerase with the TEL-patch of TPP1, recruiting telomerase to telomeres (Figure 8).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: Mutation of either interaction partner (TEN-domain or TEL-patch) results in sequestration of telomerase in Cajal bodies and failure to elongate telomeres in vivo.
source: Mutation of either interaction partner results in sequestration of telomerase in Cajal bodies and failure to elongate telomeres in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data on mutant localization and telomere length.

claim: The identification of the interface between telomerase and the telomere provides a molecular mechanism explaining the failure of previously described N-DAT mutants to function in vivo.
source: Our observations provide a molecular mechanism explaining the failure of previously described N-DAT mutants to function in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The interaction between the TEL-patch of TPP1 and the TEN-domain of hTERT provides a molecular mechanism to explain the failure of N-DAT mutations to immortalize cells.
source: The interaction between the TEL-patch of TPP1 and the TEN-domain of hTERT provides a molecular mechanism to explain the failure of N-DAT mutations to immortalize cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Charge-swap mutations on the TEN-domain of hTERT and the TEL-patch of TPP1 restore telomerase recruitment, indicating that these elements interact directly.
source: Our observation that charge-swap mutations on the TEN-domain of hTERT and the TEL-patch of TPP1 restore telomerase recruitment indicates that these elements interact directly; for other examples see Jucovic and Hartley (1996); Tansey and Herr (1997); Pennock et al. (2001).
evidence: This is supported by the charge-swap experiments and citations to similar approaches in other systems.

claim: hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K lead to similar reductions in RAP stimulation when combined with wild-type TPP1 and wild-type hTERT, respectively.
source: We note that hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K lead to similar reductions in RAP stimulation when combined with wild-type TPP1 and wild-type hTERT, respectively.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The observation that hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K lead to similar reductions in RAP stimulation adds additional support to the model that hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K eliminate reciprocal residues of the same molecular interaction.
source: This observation adds additional support to the model that hTERT K78E and TPP1 E215K eliminate reciprocal residues of the same molecular interaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The V144M mutation in hTERT and the E215K mutation in the TEL-patch of TPP1 display an additive reduction in RAP stimulation, indicating that they affect separate components of the telomerase–TPP1 interface.
source: In contrast, the V144M mutation in hTERT and the E215K mutation in the TEL-patch of TPP1 display an additive reduction in RAP stimulation, indicating that they affect separate components of the telomerase–TPP1 interface.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing additive effects.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Est3 shares structural conservation with TPP1.
source: Another variation occurs in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, where Est3 shares structural conservation with TPP1 (Yu et al., 2008; Rao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yu et al., 2008 and Rao et al., 2014.

claim: Est3 is part of the telomerase holoenzyme instead of the telomeric cap in S. cerevisiae.
source: Est3 is part of the telomerase holoenzyme instead of the telomeric cap (Hughes et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hughes et al., 2000.

claim: Est3 is thought to make direct contacts with the TEN-domain of Est2, the yeast TERT.
source: Est3 is thought to make direct contacts with the TEN-domain of Est2, the yeast TERT (Friedman et al., 2003; Talley et al., 2011; Yen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Friedman et al., 2003; Talley et al., 2011; Yen et al., 2011.

claim: Est3 appears to stimulate telomerase activity rather than act as a recruitment factor in S. cerevisiae.
source: However, Est3 appears to stimulate telomerase activity rather than act as a recruitment factor (Talley et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Talley et al., 2011.

claim: Recruitment in S. cerevisiae is mediated by the interaction of the Est1 subunit of the telomerase holoenzyme and Cdc13 at the telomere.
source: Recruitment is instead mediated by the interaction of the Est1 subunit of the telomerase holoenzyme and Cdc13 at the telomere (Evans and Lundblad, 1999), and charge-swap mutations indicate that this interaction is direct (Pennock et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Evans and Lundblad, 1999 and Pennock et al., 2001.

claim: In budding yeast the interaction between a TPP1-like OB-domain protein (Est3) and the TEN-domain of TERT (Est2) is conserved, but the recruitment mechanism differs significantly from that in humans.
source: Thus, in budding yeast the interaction between a TPP1-like OB-domain protein (Est3) and the TEN-domain of TERT (Est2) is conserved, but the recruitment mechanism differs significantly from that in humans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the mechanisms in different organisms.

claim: Depletion of TIN2 from shelterin results in a reduction of telomerase association with the telomere.
source: Depletion of TIN2 from shelterin (Abreu et al., 2010) and perturbation of the TCAB1-hTR interaction (Stern et al., 2012) both result in a reduction of telomerase association with the telomere.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abreu et al., 2010.

claim: Perturbation of the TCAB1-hTR interaction results in a reduction of telomerase association with the telomere.
source: Depletion of TIN2 from shelterin (Abreu et al., 2010) and perturbation of the TCAB1-hTR interaction (Stern et al., 2012) both result in a reduction of telomerase association with the telomere.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Stern et al., 2012.

claim: TCAB1 is necessary for telomerase maturation and trafficking to Cajal bodies.
source: TCAB1 is necessary for telomerase maturation and trafficking to Cajal bodies (Venteicher et al., 2009), while TIN2 is required for TPP1 localization to telomeres (Abreu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Venteicher et al., 2009.

claim: TIN2 is required for TPP1 localization to telomeres.
source: TCAB1 is necessary for telomerase maturation and trafficking to Cajal bodies (Venteicher et al., 2009), while TIN2 is required for TPP1 localization to telomeres (Abreu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abreu et al., 2010.

claim: Synthetic C-DAT mutants have severe activity defects.
source: However, synthetic C-DAT mutants have severe activity defects (Huard et al., 2003; Jurczyluk et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huard et al., 2003 and Jurczyluk et al., 2011.

claim: The disease-associated mutation E1117X has ∼10% of wild-type activity and appears to be sequestered to Cajal bodies in vivo.
source: E1117X has ∼10% of wild-type activity and appears to be sequestered to Cajal bodies in vivo (Tsakiri et al., 2007; Zhong et al., 2012); in contrast, F1127L has reasonable activity (∼70%) and localizes to telomeres, and it is stimulated by POT1-TPP1 (Zhong et al., 2012; Zaug et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tsakiri et al., 2007 and Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: The disease-associated mutation F1127L has reasonable activity (∼70%) and localizes to telomeres, and it is stimulated by POT1-TPP1.
source: E1117X has ∼10% of wild-type activity and appears to be sequestered to Cajal bodies in vivo (Tsakiri et al., 2007; Zhong et al., 2012); in contrast, F1127L has reasonable activity (∼70%) and localizes to telomeres, and it is stimulated by POT1-TPP1 (Zhong et al., 2012; Zaug et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhong et al., 2012 and Zaug et al., 2013.

claim: CTE mutants do not have clear recruitment defects dissociated from activity loss.
source: Thus, CTE mutants do not have clear recruitment defects dissociated from activity loss, despite their importance based on disease association.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of CTE mutants.

claim: A mutant TPP1-OB-domain increases the localization of a mutant hTERT to a non-telomeric locus in vivo, while it strongly decreases the association with wild-type hTERT.
source: In contrast, the observation that a mutant TPP1-OB-domain increases the localization of a mutant hTERT to a non-telomeric locus in vivo, while it strongly decreases the association with wild-type hTERT, demonstrates that a direct TEN-domain-TEL-patch interaction is necessary and may be sufficient for telomerase recruitment to telomeres in humans.
evidence: This is supported by the LacI assay data.

claim: A direct TEN-domain-TEL-patch interaction is necessary and may be sufficient for telomerase recruitment to telomeres in humans.
source: In contrast, the observation that a mutant TPP1-OB-domain increases the localization of a mutant hTERT to a non-telomeric locus in vivo, while it strongly decreases the association with wild-type hTERT, demonstrates that a direct TEN-domain-TEL-patch interaction is necessary and may be sufficient for telomerase recruitment to telomeres in humans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Multiple disease mutations associated with IPF—P33S, L55Q, Pro112ProfsX16, and V144M—cluster in TEN-domain of hTERT.
source: Multiple disease mutations associated with IPF—P33S, L55Q, Pro112ProfsX16, and V144M—cluster in TEN-domain of hTERT.
evidence: This is a statement about the location of disease mutations.

claim: Mutation carriers of IPF-associated TEN-domain mutations have significantly shorter telomeres than non-carrier relatives.
source: Mutation carriers have significantly shorter telomeres than non-carrier relatives (Armanios et al., 2007; Tsakiri et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Armanios et al., 2007 and Tsakiri et al., 2007.

claim: IPF-associated TEN-domain mutations have variable impacts on telomerase enzymatic activity.
source: These mutations have variable impacts on telomerase enzymatic activity (Armanios et al., 2007; Tsakiri et al., 2007; Zaug et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Armanios et al., 2007; Tsakiri et al., 2007; Zaug et al., 2013.

claim: V144M is defective in TPP1-mediated RAP stimulation in vitro.
source: Importantly, V144M is defective in TPP1-mediated RAP stimulation in vitro (this study) and fails to localize to telomeres in vivo (Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by data from this study.

claim: V144M fails to localize to telomeres in vivo.
source: Importantly, V144M is defective in TPP1-mediated RAP stimulation in vitro (this study) and fails to localize to telomeres in vivo (Zhong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: It is likely that some cases of IPF are directly caused by a decrease in telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
source: Given the propensity of both synthetic and IPF-associated mutations in the TEN-domain of hTERT to disrupt telomere localization, it is likely that some cases of IPF are directly caused by a decrease in telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of disease mutations.

claim: Agonists of the TEL-patch-TEN-domain interaction that compensated for IPF-associated mutations and attenuated telomere shortening might be pharmaceutically important.
source: Agonists of the TEL-patch-TEN-domain interaction that compensated for these mutations and attenuated telomere shortening associated with the disease might be pharmaceutically important.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Reactivation of telomerase is a hallmark of most human cancers.
source: In contrast to the loss of telomerase function associated with IPF, reactivation of telomerase is a hallmark of most human cancers.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Inhibitors that disrupt telomerase recruitment to telomeres would provide an additional approach to target telomerase activity in cancer cells.
source: Inhibitors that disrupt telomerase recruitment to telomeres would provide an additional approach to target telomerase activity in cancer cells.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Disruption of the TEL-patch diminishes cell growth and triggers apoptosis in HeLa cells.
source: In support of this idea, disruption of the TEL-patch diminishes cell growth and triggers apoptosis in HeLa cells, and this effect is exacerbated in combination with a small molecule inhibitor of telomerase activity (Nakashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nakashima et al., 2013.

claim: The effect of TEL-patch disruption on cell growth is exacerbated in combination with a small molecule inhibitor of telomerase activity.
source: In support of this idea, disruption of the TEL-patch diminishes cell growth and triggers apoptosis in HeLa cells, and this effect is exacerbated in combination with a small molecule inhibitor of telomerase activity (Nakashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nakashima et al., 2013.

claim: The finding that the TEN-domain of hTERT interacts directly with the TEL-patch of TPP1 defines a key interface and provides a direct target for the design of novel therapeutic inhibitors of telomerase action.
source: Our finding that the TEN-domain of hTERT interacts directly with the TEL-patch of TPP1 to bring telomerase to the telomere defines a key interface and provides a direct target for the design of novel therapeutic inhibitors of telomerase action.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the therapeutic implications of the study's findings.

claim: Wild-type telomerase localized to telomeres and promoted the formation of neo-Cajal bodies at most telomeres, as shown by the co-localization of TRF2, hTERT, and coilin foci.
source: As previously described (Zhong et al., 2012), wild-type telomerase localized to telomeres and promoted the formation of neo-Cajal bodies at most telomeres, as shown by the co-localization of TRF2, hTERT, and coilin foci (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Zhong et al., 2012.

claim: Expression of wild-type hTERT caused a progressive increase in telomere length to ∼14.8 kb.
source: Expression of wild-type hTERT caused a progressive increase in telomere length to ∼14.8 kb (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The telomere length of the parental HeLa cell line was stable over the course of the experiment at ∼6.6 kb.
source: The telomere length of the parental HeLa cell line was stable over the course of the experiment at ∼6.6 kb (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Overexpression of hTERT alone leads to a moderate increase in telomerase activity per cell, more closely resembling endogenous telomerase levels than those obtained by overexpression of both hTERT and hTR.
source: Overexpression of hTERT alone leads to a moderate increase in telomerase activity per cell, more closely resembling endogenous telomerase levels than those obtained by overexpression of both hTERT and hTR (Cristofari et al., 2007; Xi and Cech, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cristofari et al., 2007 and Xi and Cech, 2014.

claim: Telomerase immuno-purified from stable cell lines expressing mCherry-hTERT variants had comparable activities per cell, and these activity levels were threefold to fourfold higher than levels in untransfected control cells.
source: Thus, while the absolute expression level of mCherry-hTERT varied between the stable cell lines (Figure 4A), telomerase immuno-purified from the cell lines had comparable activities per cell, and these activity levels were threefold to fourfold higher than levels in untransfected control cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: All mutant POT1-TPP1 complexes had identical elution profiles from the sizing column.
source: All mutant POT1-TPP1 complexes had identical elution profiles from the sizing column (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The presence of a single elution peak indicated that all TEL-patch mutant TPP1 proteins were not globally misfolded and formed heterodimers with POT1.
source: The presence of a single elution peak indicated that all TEL-patch mutant TPP1 proteins were not globally misfolded and formed heterodimers with POT1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the gel filtration data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: TPP1 E169K gave dramatic reductions in RAP and did not stimulate any of the tested telomerases above 24% of wild-type.
source: TPP1 E169K gave dramatic reductions in RAP and did not stimulate any of the tested telomerases above 24% of wild-type (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: hTERT mutant R132E and the double mutant K78E;R132E were stimulated at levels less than 23% of wild-type by all TPP1 proteins tested.
source: hTERT mutant R132E and the double mutant K78E;R132E were stimulated at levels less than 23% of wild-type by all TPP1 proteins tested (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: The charge-swap rescue was statistically significant when using telomerase from rabbit reticulocyte lysates (RRLs).
source: Furthermore, to rule out the possibility of a bridging factor that co-purifies with telomerase from HEK293 T cells, we carried out the charge-swap experiment with telomerase purified from rabbit reticulocyte lysates (RRLs). The charge-swap rescue was statistically significant when using telomerase from RRLs, although the absolute PT stimulation of RRL telomerase was diminished (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: V144M telomerase retained moderate telomerase activity and high processivity (48% and 95% of wild-type telomerase, respectively) but POT1-TPP1 RAP stimulation was significantly decreased to 61% when compared to wild-type telomerase.
source: V144M telomerase retained moderate telomerase activity and high processivity (48% and 95% of wild-type telomerase, respectively) but POT1-TPP1 RAP stimulation was significantly decreased to 61% when compared to wild-type telomerase (Table 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: TEL patch mutants E169K and E215K each resulted in an additive loss of RAP stimulation when tested with disease mutant V144M, to 28% and 37% respectively.
source: Furthermore, TEL patch mutants E169K and E215K each resulted in an additive loss of RAP stimulation when tested with disease mutant V144M, to 28% and 37% respectively (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Wild-type telomerase co-localized with the TPP1-OB-fold domain in ∼90% of nuclei.
source: Wild-type telomerase co-localized with the TPP1-OB-fold domain in ∼90% of nuclei.
evidence: This is supported by the LacI assay data.

claim: In cells expressing K78E, R132E, or K78E;R132E telomerase, the fraction of TPP1-OB-fold domain foci showing telomerase signal was reduced to ∼55%, ∼30%, and 0%, respectively.
source: In contrast, in cells expressing K78E, R132E, or K78E;R132E telomerase, the fraction of TPP1-OB-fold domain foci showing telomerase signal was reduced to ∼55%, ∼30%, and 0%, respectively (Figure 6B,C, additional examples in Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B, 6C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduction in co-localization demonstrated that mutation of the hTERT TEN-domain interferes with the interaction between telomerase and the TPP1-OB-fold domain in vivo.
source: The reduction in co-localization demonstrated that mutation of the hTERT TEN-domain interferes with the interaction between telomerase and the TPP1-OB-fold domain in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LacI assay data.

claim: Telomere length in the cell line expressing only K78E hTERT was constant at ∼3.4 kb during the 6-week experiment.
source: Telomere length in the cell line expressing only K78E hTERT was constant at ∼3.4 kb during the 6-week experiment.
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data.

claim: Expression of WT TPP1 led to an increase of telomere length to ∼6.2 kb in cells expressing K78E hTERT.
source: Expression of WT TPP1 led to an increase of telomere length to ∼6.2 kb.
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data.

claim: Expression of E169K TPP1 led to a subtle increase in telomere length to ∼4.9 kb in cells expressing K78E hTERT.
source: Importantly, expression of E215K TPP1 triggered a more pronounced increase in telomere length to ∼7.7 kb over the same time period, while E169K gave lead to a subtle increase to ∼4.9 kb.
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data.
